answer: A harbor registry resists sybils by making each identity expensive to moor: registration requires a refundable bond plus a device-bound attestation checked by independent verifiers. One attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must post a thousand bonds and pass a thousand checks, while an honest agent pays once. Reputation then grows slowly, like a reef, through sustained useful work, not instantly. A velvet-smooth signup with no cost or check would let a single operator dock a whole fleet of sock puppets.
